Summary (proposed):
- Acceptance criteria:
  * Median latency (token gen) under 120ms US, 140ms EU, 160ms APAC for typical prompt mix
  * TTFT (time-to-first-token) under 180ms across regions at 95th pct
  * Sustained concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions per model replica, target aggregate throughput 5k tokens/sec per pool
- Verification sprint: 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-24 (short smoke + load sweep)
- Failover tests: controlled region blackout + warm/cold fallback routing; measure failover completion and request loss
- Deliverables: CSV of raw latency sweeps, consolidated readout, failover trace screenshots, MAP sign-off checklist

Attachments: map-runbook.xlsx (run steps + responsibilities)

Subject: MAP readout: sprint results and recommended close timeline

Team — thanks for the collaboration. Final readout summary below (full CSVs and traces attached / Drive link above):

Executive summary:
- Latency (median token gen): US 98ms, EU 125ms, APAC 152ms (all within proposed thresholds)
- TTFT (95th pct across payload buckets): short 110ms, mid 155ms, long 210ms (long prompts exceed the 180ms target; see recommendation)
- Sustained throughput: achieved ~5.2k tokens/sec aggregated across pooled replicas at 200 concurrent sessions (above target)
- KV cache hit rates: US 78%, EU 72%, APAC 59% — cache hit materially improved apparent TTFT in US/EU; APAC worst due to cold-started prefix sets
- Failover behavior: on simulated APAC region degradation, automated routing shifted 98% of new requests to EU/US within 18s; TTFT spiked ~350ms during the switch window with ~0.12% request error rate (retries recovered most lost responses)

Recommendations / next steps for MAP sign-off:
1) For long-prompt TTFT, enable aggressive KV pre-warming for APAC (we can run a short pre-warm job to improve from 59% to ~75%, estimate 12–18% TTFT reduction).
2) Add a 30-minute run with warm caches in APAC to validate pre-warm benefit — schedule next week if you want hard numbers before PO.
3) Include failover SLO exception in the contract for <30s transient spikes during region failover, with post-mortem deliverable for any incident.
4) Proposed close timeline: PO submission 2026-05-05, contract signature 2026-05-12, launch window 2026-06-01 (private deployment/onsite integration to follow in June).

Attachments: failover-trace.png (screenshot of routing graph), latency-sweep-results.csv (final), map-runbook.xlsx (updated with actual timings)

Please reply with any objections; otherwise we'll draft the MAP sign-off doc and the SOW addendum for the timeline above.

— Lauren Bishop
VP Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
